first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates that shorter onboarding improves completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. Promotional pricing directly addresses competitive pressure, but its documented 30-day retention harm conflicts with the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Verify the most directly relevant onboarding evidence and the pricing downside before committing the single experiment slot.

final.rationale: Run shortened onboarding only for simple self-serve accounts, explicitly excluding complex-workspace accounts. This directly addresses the current completion and activation declines and has demonstrated gains in completion and time-to-value. The guarded scope avoids the identified 60-day churn harm in complex workspaces. Promotional pricing is rejected despite competitive pressure because its acquired cohorts showed materially worse first-renewal retention, conflicting with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Measure activation, qualified revenue, and retention rather than treating early completion as sufficient.
